portfolioFeatures.title: Redux Web and Native Application Development
portfolioFeatures.description: I develop custom Redux web and native applications using the latest Expo and React Native technologies. I use RTK Query for data fetching and Redux Toolkit for state management.

portfolioFeatures.title: UX and UI Development
portfolioFeatures.description: I develop custom UX and UI designs for web and mobile applications.

appProcedures.title: Data Flow and Logic
appProcedures.description: No hardcoded data is to live in component or slice files. Data is fetched from the API and stored in the Redux store. The data is then used by the components through their respective slices and reducers. https://redux.js.org/style-guide/#put-as-much-logic-as-possible-in-reducers

appProcedures.title: Theming
appProcedures.description: Theming is implemented using the Tamagui library. The theme is stored in the Redux store and is used by the components. Theme files are located in the src/styles/themes directory using a theme-<themeName>.css naming convention. There is a theme toggle button in the navigation bar that allows the user to switch between themes that are dynamically loaded from the src/styles/themes directory. There is a theme template download button and theme load button for loading custom themes.

appProcedures.title: Routing
appProcedures.description: Routing is implemented using the Expo Router library. The routing is stored in the Redux store and is used by the components.

appProcedures.title: Data
appProcedures.description: The data flow is API-owned JSON > RTK Query cache > listener > entity slice > selector > view. Portfolio runtime code contains no bundled content fallback; API contract types live beside the API boundary.

about.headline: I build systems that think locally.
about.statement: Twelve years of shipping, most of it spent on the awkward seams: game engines that need to reason without a network, one codebase that has to be native on three platforms, and functional cores that keep their shape whether they are written in TypeScript, C++ or Haskell.

domains.title: Local-first neuro-symbolic AI
domains.summary: NPC engines that reason on the player's machine — no round trip, no rented inference.
domains.detail: ForbocAI builds dialogue, memory-aware interaction and validated action for game worlds, shipped as an Unreal Engine SDK with a visual authoring studio and a hosted API behind it.

domains.title: Functional cores, four languages deep
domains.summary: The same algebra — Maybe, Either, folds, dispatch tables — ported rather than reinvented.
domains.detail: A cyber-noir MUD written entirely in Vimscript on a pure functional architecture, API templates in Haskell, and an Unreal SDK whose data boundaries are composed rather than branched.

domains.title: Universal applications
domains.summary: One Expo codebase that is genuinely native on iOS and Android, and static on the web.
domains.detail: Redux Toolkit for state, RTK Query for the server cache, Tamagui for a design system that compiles to both. This site is the reference implementation — read its source, then scan the QR.

domains.title: Automation that removes a job, not a step
domains.summary: Pipelines that take a brief in and hand finished work back.
domains.detail: Campaign briefs resolved into multi-format creative through generative imaging, disposable telephony with numbers released the moment a message lands, and agent skills for legal workflows.

principles.title: Composition over branching
principles.description: Route by shape or by key. A dispatch table beats a ternary chain, and a fold beats a loop.

principles.title: Reducers stay pure
principles.description: Effects live at the edges — RTK Query for server cache, listeners for reactive work.

principles.title: Explicit boundaries by default
principles.description: The API is the only content authority. A dead network produces an honest degraded state instead of silently substituting stale bundled copy.

principles.title: Evidence over assertion
principles.description: Every claim on this page links to the repository that backs it.
